claims.text: Laser surface melting with high-speed laser scanning will refine the microstructure of Inconel 718.
Laser surface melting will reduce segregation of Nb-rich phases in Inconel 718.
Rapid solidification occurs during the proposed laser surface-melting process.
Epitaxial growth occurs during the proposed laser surface-melting process.
Rapid solidification, epitaxial growth, microstructural refinement, and reduced Nb-rich segregation will reduce the hot-cracking susceptibility of Inconel 718.
The treated surface will have greater resistance to hot cracking than a traditional fusion-welding repair.
The treated surface will have greater resistance to hot cracking than an untreated Inconel 718 surface.
Laser surface melting will increase the surface hardness of Inconel 718 relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and the untreated surface.
Improved hot-cracking resistance and surface hardness will reduce the risk of surface-defect initiation.
A laser power of 2 kW and scanning speed of 100 mm/s are suitable operating conditions for the proposed treatment.
The proposed treatment uses argon shielding gas.
Optimized scanning parameters and post-treatment heat management will promote a uniform microstructure.
Optimized scanning parameters and post-treatment heat management will minimize residual stresses.
The proposed surface treatment is intended for service involving high temperature, corrosion, and wear.
